summary: Tested Spell System Overhaul Batch C: backend PUT merge semantics (6 pytest cases, all green) and frontend SpellManager interactive flows via Playwright (DM edit + anon read-only, all green). One UI rendering bug spotted in the legacy details card that displays spell_slots_used as '[object Object]'. One latent backend defect identified: PUT /api/pcs/{id} with body omitting `level` resets level to 1 (Pydantic default). The live frontend works around this because SpellManager spreads the full metadata, but it should be hardened.

minor.issue: If client omits `level`, Pydantic defaults body.level=1 and backend overwrites the stored level to 1 (since `body.level if body.level is not None else metadata.get(...)`). Same risk for any other field whose Pydantic default is non-None (e.g. level). Frontend SpellManager mitigates by spreading full metadata, but any other minimal-PUT consumer (or a future refactor) would silently corrupt the character. Recommended fix: change PlayerCharacterIn.level default to None, like the other 5e fields, and use the unified `if v is not None` merge pattern.

ui_bugs.issue: The top properties card renders `spell_slots_used` metadata as raw '[object Object]'. The generic key/value renderer cannot stringify the dict. Either hide internal keys (spell_slots_used, spells_prepared, spells_known, spell_slots, ability_scores, resource_*) from the legacy details card, or format them. Visible on /characters/<slug>.

action_items: Hide or pretty-print object-valued metadata keys (spell_slots_used, spell_slots, ability_scores, spells_prepared, spells_known) in EntryDetail's legacy properties card; they're already rendered by the new SpellManager/CharacterSheet so the duplication shows '[object Object]'.
Optional hardening: change PlayerCharacterIn.level default from 1 to None and merge with the unified `if v is not None` block so minimal PUT bodies cannot accidentally reset level.
critical_code_review_comments: PlayerCharacterIn defines `level: Optional[int] = 1`, but the PUT merge treats `body.level` as authoritative when not None (which is always, due to the default). This is inconsistent with race/class which use `body.race or metadata.get('race', '')`. Move level into the `if v is not None` loop with a None default.

SpellManager.persist() spreads `...m` (raw metadata) into the PUT payload — this works only because PlayerCharacterIn has `extra='ignore'`. It also re-sends `class` (which won't map to `char_class`), `owner`, `user_id`, etc. Mostly harmless thanks to `extra='ignore'` and the fall-back-to-existing branches, but it's a fragile contract. Consider an explicit allow-list in the frontend, or a dedicated PATCH endpoint for slot/prepared updates.
seed_data_creation: Test PC `TEST_UIWizard` (slug test-uiwizard) created via API for the Playwright run and deleted in teardown. Backend test_spells.py auto-creates and deletes TEST_Wizard_<uuid> PCs.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Batch C functionality (interactive pips + long rest + prepared toggle + read-only anon view) is fully working end-to-end. Two non-blocking issues remain: (1) legacy EntryDetail meta card shows '[object Object]' for spell_slots_used; (2) backend PUT silently resets `level` to 1 if omitted — only triggered by a minimal PUT, not by the current SpellManager flow. Re-use /app/backend/tests/test_spells.py for regression; it covers create, slot merge, prepared merge, long rest, anon 403, and public GET visibility.
rca of the issue: EntryDetail '[object Object]' bug: a generic key→value renderer in the character details card stringifies `spell_slots_used` (a dict) using default JS coercion. Fix by either omitting structured keys from the iterator or JSON.stringify-ing object values. PUT level reset RCA: PlayerCharacterIn declares `level: Optional[int] = 1` while race/class default to '' and are merged via truthy fallback; level uses an `is not None` check so the default 1 always wins over existing metadata.level. Move level into the unified `if v is not None` block (same pattern as max_hp, armor_class).
